name: charactercheck
description: Deterministic D&D Beyond character-sheet derivation with provenance. Input: a public DDB character URL/id (or saved v5 JSON). Output: derived stats where every value carries its arithmetic, plus honest lanes: 'unhandled' (recognized-but-unmodeled data, named) and 'lint' (sheet inconsistencies).

commands.charactercheck derive <ref>: full derived character as JSON (the main entry point)
commands.charactercheck stance <ref>: pre-combat: hands, AC states with costs, attack lines
commands.charactercheck seatpack <ref> [--for-dm]: everything a seat needs before a session
commands.charactercheck quiz <ref>: settlement questions the GM asks aloud, with expected values
commands.charactercheck diff <ref> --baseline <sn: what the player changed mid-session (state vs build vs impossible)
commands.charactercheck report <ref>: unhandled + lint only — resolve these before play
commands.charactercheck doctor [ref] [--json]: diagnose why it is not working: python, DNS, outbound HTTPS, and character reachability. PASS/FAIL per check with the remedy on the first failure. Exit 0 all-pass, 3 otherwise.
commands.charactercheck selftest: prove the engine works offline against a bundled sample character — no network, no account, no character required. Exit 0 pass, 1 fail. Run this FIRST when bootstrapping: it separates 'the tool is broken' from 'I cannot reach that character'.

exit_codes.1: lint findings — the sheet disagrees with itself; output still usable
exit_codes.2: unhandled content present — NOT a failure; output complete and usable, resolve named items with a human
exit_codes.3: could not retrieve the sheet — read the 'action' field; private sheet, bad id, or no network

boundaries: Derivation and extraction only: no rules adjudication (see srdcheck), no auth/cookies (public sheets only), no VTT output, no homebrew content database. Unrecognized data is reported by name, never silently defaulted.

errors.note: Every failure prints structured JSON with a stable 'error' kind and a one-sentence 'action'. Never a traceback. charactercheck never asks for credentials: a private sheet is answered by making it public or by passing a saved character-service JSON file.
